points.t: A woman distressed by **terminal hair** on the face, chest, abdomen or back.
**Androgen excess** (ovary, adrenal, drugs) or **increased follicle sensitivity** to normal androgens (idiopathic).
Score and record impact, check **testosterone**, screen for PCOS; hair removal + **COC**; specialist anti-androgens with contraception.
**Rapid-onset virilisation** (deep voice, clitoromegaly, testosterone > 5 nmol/L): androgen-secreting tumour.

cause.lead: Androgens turn soft vellus hair into coarse terminal hair.
points: 5α-reductase in the follicle converts testosterone to **DHT**.
Less common: **NC-CAH** (17-OH-progesterone), Cushing’s, acromegaly, prolactin, thyroid; **androgen-secreting tumours**; drugs (anabolic steroids, testosterone, danazol, valproate).
**Hypertrichosis** is different: non-androgen pattern (ciclosporin, minoxidil, phenytoin).

visuals.caption: Under androgen influence a fine pale vellus hair (left) becomes a thick, dark terminal hair from a larger, deeper follicle (right).
visuals.alt: Skin sections showing vellus and terminal hair follicles

features.lead: Score it, but listen to the distress.
points: Male-pattern sites: upper lip, chin, jawline, chest, abdomen, back, thighs.
**mFG**: 9 areas scored 0–4 (total 0–36); **≥ 8** traditional cut-off, **≥ 4–6** in some populations.
‘**Patient-important hirsutism**’: localised distressing hair even with a low total.
Limits: subjective; underestimates after hair removal; no extra weight for the face.
Onset and pace, cycles, fertility, weight, drugs and supplements, family.
Virilisation, acne, acanthosis nigricans, Cushingoid signs.
Regular cycles (may be anovulatory) or normal testosterone (20–30%).

cards.name: Idiopathic
cards.clue: Slow, peripubertal; regular cycles; normal androgens.

cards.name: PCOS
cards.clue: Oligo-/anovulation, mild ↑ T, ↓ SHBG, AN, obesity, acne.

manage.lead: Layer treatments; hormonal effects take 6–12 months.

points: **Weight loss** (even 5% improves SHBG and androgens), exercise; PCOS / metabolic risk.
Shaving (doesn’t thicken hair), plucking, threading, waxing (folliculitis, PIH), creams, bleaching.
Laser / IPL (dark hair, light skin; Nd:YAG for darker skin), electrolysis. NHS funding limited.
First-line systemic if distress persists after ≥ 6 months: ↓ ovarian androgen, ↑ SHBG; a low-VTE levonorgestrel pill is a reasonable start.
Eflornithine cream discontinued in the UK: check availability.
Spironolactone 50–200 mg/day, cyproterone, finasteride: **off-label, specialist-advised**, with reliable contraception.

visuals.caption: Laser or IPL hair removal works best on dark hair and light skin (Nd:YAG for darker skin) and needs several sessions; eye protection is essential. NHS funding is limited.
visuals.alt: Woman with goggles having laser hair removal on the chin

limits.t: Anti-androgens can feminise a male fetus: effective contraception essential.

items.t: Rapid onset over months, virilisation or very high testosterone: **urgent endocrine** referral.
Suspected NC-CAH, Cushing’s or other endocrine cause.

pearls.t: Hormones stop **new** coarsening; they don’t remove existing hair: combine with removal.
Shaving is safe and doesn’t make regrowth thicker.
Ask about a partner’s **testosterone gel**, anabolic steroids, valproate.

quiz.a: Rapid onset with virilisation or testosterone > 5 nmol/L.
A combined oral contraceptive, after ≥ 6 months of cosmetic measures.
